# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 81 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 81 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_081_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 8 — The Taxonomy Completed

**1** "What about those who returned two-thirds-green and one-third-withered branches?" I asked. "These were believers," he said, "but some of them fell away from the faith and are now turning back to God. **2** They will live — their repentance is genuine, and they will not be lost. But those who fell away and haven't repented will perish." **3** "And those who returned two-thirds-withered and one-third-green branches?" **4** "These believed, but were for the most part wavering and uncertain — many were wealthy and caught up in worldly affairs, which eroded their commitment to God. They put their business dealings first. Yet they never fully abandoned God — there was always a small ember of faith still burning in them." **5** "And those with a tiny bit of green and almost entirely withered branches? They were deeply wavering, full of doubt, and their actions showed it." **6** "Those who returned completely dried-out and worm-eaten branches," he said, "are those who walked away from the Lord entirely and never returned." **7** "And those with only a trace of green and the rest dried out — these are people who heard God's word and believed, but couldn't commit wholeheartedly to the Lord and never consistently lived rightly. They were somewhere in between — not gone, but not truly living either." **8** "Lord," I asked, "who actually qualifies to live in the tower?" "Only those," he said, "who returned their branches completely green — people who never cut themselves off from the living God, who held their faith firm and didn't let the world seep in, who remained unstained and lived righteously in everything they did."

---

*PNEUMA renders "double-minded" as "wavering and uncertain" to make the concept accessible. The tower qualification in v. 8 is the climactic summary of Similitude 8's taxonomy.*
